newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia ready to start talks on NATO charter.
newsitem.headline: Russia ready to start talks on NATO charter.

text.p: Russia indicated on Tuesday it was ready to start talks with NATO on a charter governing all aspects of the relationship between the two former Cold War foes, a NATO official said.

He told reporters Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov had asked when Moscow could start the dialogue during a meeting with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana despite the alliance's decision to press ahead with eastwards expansion.

Russia bitterly opposes the alliance's plans to grant membership to at least some countries in former communist central and eastern Europe. NATO foreign ministers on Tuesday called a special summit in Madrid next July to invite candidate countries to open accession talks.

They said they wanted the same summit to endorse a new "strong, stable and enduring security partnership" between Russia and the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) and authorised Solana to open talks on the issue with Moscow.

"It is interesting that they (the Russians) are now indicating a willingness to talk to us on the essentials. They are no longer asking us to change the enlargement policy before they can talk," said the official.
He said Primakov had not referred to enlargement during his brief 20-minute meeting with Solana. He is due to meet NATO foreign ministers for more substantive talks on Wednesday.
